title: Preferred audio latency is below 15 ms
evidence: Lower values will result in lower audio latency at the cost of increased CPU usage
suggestion: Raise audio/driver/output_latency toward 15 if you hear crackling or the mix thread is hot. The description says low values cost CPU and can crackle.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: Audio buses stay awake at quieter levels than the default
evidence: This saves CPU as effects assigned to that bus will no longer do any processing
suggestion: Move audio/buses/channel_disable_threshold_db up toward -60 so idle buses disable. The description says disabling the bus skips its effects.
tradeoff: Very quiet tails get cut sooner.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: Audio buses wait longer than 2 seconds before disabling
evidence: This saves CPU as effects assigned to that bus will no longer do any processing
suggestion: Lower audio/buses/channel_disable_time toward the default 2 seconds. A longer window keeps effects running after the sound has dropped.
tradeoff: Short gaps in a loop may click if the bus sleeps.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: Text-to-speech support is enabled
evidence: idle CPU usage and interfere with the sleep mode
suggestion: Turn audio/general/text_to_speech off when the game does not speak. The description warns about idle CPU use and sleep mode.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: An audio player allows more than one voice
heuristic_rationale: The class says max_polyphony is how many sounds play at once and that extra sounds cut off the oldest. Above the default of 1 means more simultaneous mixes. No voice budget is documented.
evidence: The maximum number of sounds this node can play at the same time
suggestion: Lower max_polyphony toward 1 on players that do not need overlapping sounds. The class says extra sounds cut off the oldest.
expected_effect: scan_scene should show a lower count after the edit. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: An active or autoplay 3D sound has no distance cutoff
heuristic_rationale: An assigned stream is playing or configured to autoplay. This does not prove it is currently distant, audible or expensive.
evidence: requiring audio mixing when the listener is far away, which saves CPU resources.
suggestion: For local sounds, compare a finite audible distance and profile CPU audio work with the listener moving through the scene.
tradeoff: A cutoff changes the fade and removes distant sound; preserve intentionally far-reaching ambience.
expected_effect: scan_scene should show a lower count after the edit. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: Measured audio output latency is above 50 ms
heuristic_rationale: The monitor is AudioServer output latency in seconds. 50 ms is above the 15 ms preferred default of audio/driver/output_latency. It is not a hardware measurement from this tool.
evidence: it is not recommended to call this every frame
suggestion: AUDIO_OUTPUT_LATENCY is the measured output latency in seconds. Compare it with audio/driver/output_latency. The class says not to query it every frame.
tradeoff: Depends on which objects or allocations you remove.
expected_effect: The same Performance monitor should fall on the next collect_metrics.

title: A dry-only reverb still processes its filter network
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled native AudioEffectReverb on a non-bypassed current audio bus has wet exactly 0 and dry exactly 1. Both checked versions call the reverb processor for each stereo channel, and its comb/all-pass loops run before the final wet/dry mix. There is no zero-wet bypass in that path. Bus activity is unknown; scripted/custom effects are skipped. This is a configured processing candidate, not measured CPU cost.
suggestion: Compare bypassing this effect if the wet mix stays zero and later automation does not need the reverb's warmed tail.
tradeoff: Bypassing stops updating delay/filter history. Re-enabling later can change the tail or transients; preserve intentionally warmed effects and verify the complete mix.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Compare the same active audio mix on target hardware, listening for quality changes and underruns while measuring CPU/frame timing. Runtime code may replace the editor's bus layout.

title: A neutral stereo-enhancement effect still processes samples
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled native AudioEffectStereoEnhance on a non-bypassed current audio bus has pan_pullout exactly 1, time_pullout_ms exactly 0 and surround exactly 0. The source still computes center/side channels and writes and reads the delay ring for every sample. These settings request no stereo enhancement; this does not assert bit-identical floating-point output or prove that the bus is active. Scripted/custom effects are skipped.
suggestion: Compare bypassing this effect when these neutral settings stay fixed throughout the workload.
tradeoff: Runtime pan/delay/surround automation may need the effect and its delay history. Bypass can change floating-point rounding and later transients; listen to the full mix.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Compare the same active audio mix on target hardware, listening for quality changes and underruns while measuring CPU/frame timing. Runtime code may replace the editor's bus layout.

title: An audio equalizer processes more than ten bands
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled native AudioEffectEQ6/EQ10/EQ21 on a non-bypassed current audio bus reports more than ten bands. The native EQ loop processes every band for both channels on every sample, including bands whose gain is 0 dB. The cutoff distinguishes the 21-band resource from the 6/10-band alternatives; it is a review heuristic, not a device limit. Flat gains are not assumed to make the filter bank an identity operation. Bus activity and actual CPU cost are unknown; scripted/custom effects are skipped.
suggestion: Compare EQ6 or EQ10 where the mix does not need 21 separately adjustable bands, retuning the replacement by ear or against an audio reference.
tradeoff: Fewer bands change frequency resolution and filter response. Do not copy gain numbers between different band layouts or assume a flat EQ is equivalent to bypass.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Compare the same active audio mix on target hardware, listening for quality changes and underruns while measuring CPU/frame timing. Runtime code may replace the editor's bus layout.

title: A spectrum analyzer is configured with more than four seconds of history
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: A native AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer on the current audio layout has a finite buffer_length above four seconds. AudioServer creates effect instances independently of bypass/enable state; disabling an effect or bypassing its bus does not release this history, so those states remain eligible. Instantiation allocates floor(buffer_length / (fft_size / mix_rate)) + 1 history arrays, each holding fft_size stereo AudioFrame values. This history grows roughly with duration and mix rate; a longer history does not by itself increase the FFT execution rate. Four seconds is a review cutoff matching the inspector range, not a native limit. Existing instances retain the history allocated at creation; this rule describes resource configuration. Scripted/custom effects are skipped.
suggestion: Compare the default two seconds or the shortest history that preserves the application's spectrum queries and audio/display latency tolerance, then recreate or reload the effect.
tradeoff: Shorter history can remove spectra needed by delayed visualization or analysis. Changing the resource alone does not resize an existing instance; verify the consumer after recreation.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Recreate/reload the configured analyzer, compare process memory under the same mix, and verify spectrum queries and display timing. Do not infer a CPU or frame-time saving from history duration alone. Runtime code may replace the editor's audio layout.

title: A pitch-shift effect increases FFT oversampling
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled native AudioEffectPitchShift on a non-bypassed current audio bus has a non-unity pitch scale and oversampling above its default of 4. The source shortens the FFT hop as oversampling increases; Godot documents the higher CPU demand. Unity pitch bypasses this work and is excluded. Zero-hop configurations receive a separate correctness finding. This is a configured processing path, not proof the bus is receiving audio or causing frame-time cost. Scripted/custom effects are skipped.
suggestion: Compare the default oversampling of 4 or the lowest value that preserves acceptable pitch-shift quality under the intended mix.
tradeoff: Lower oversampling can add pitch-shift artifacts. Preserve automated pitch/quality changes and test during the loudest or busiest mix.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Compare the same active audio mix on target hardware, listening for quality changes and underruns while measuring CPU/frame timing. Runtime code may replace the editor's bus layout.

title: A chorus effect processes more than two voices
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled native AudioEffectChorus on a non-bypassed current audio bus requests a nonzero wet mix and more than two voices with nonzero cutoff. Each such voice enters its own sample-processing loop. A zero cutoff skips that voice in both checked versions and is excluded. Two voices is the resource default, not a hardware limit; current configuration does not prove audible processing or measured cost.
suggestion: Compare two chorus voices or fewer on buses where the extra modulation is not audible in the complete mix.
tradeoff: Reducing voices changes modulation, stereo width and texture. Preserve intentional layering and any runtime voice automation.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Compare the same active audio mix on target hardware, listening for quality changes and underruns while measuring CPU/frame timing. Runtime code may replace the editor's bus layout.

title: A dry-only chorus still has voice processing configured
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled native AudioEffectChorus on a non-bypassed current audio bus has wet exactly 0, dry exactly 1 and at least one voice with nonzero cutoff. The native voice loop still runs when wet is zero, even though no wet contribution is requested. Bus activity is unknown; this is a measurement candidate. Scripted/custom effects are skipped.
suggestion: Compare bypassing this effect if the wet mix remains zero throughout the workload. Keep it active when upcoming automation needs its warmed delay/filter history.
tradeoff: Bypassing freezes the chorus history and phase; enabling it later can change transients. Do not remove an intentionally warmed effect used by future automation.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Compare the same active audio mix on target hardware, listening for quality changes and underruns while measuring CPU/frame timing. Runtime code may replace the editor's bus layout.

title: A microphone stream is used while audio input is off
evidence: Godot prints "You must enable the project setting "audio/driver/enable_input" to use audio capture." when an AudioStreamMicrophone starts while audio/driver/enable_input is off; nothing is captured.
suggestion: Enable audio/driver/enable_input (export templates may also need microphone permissions on mobile and web).
tradeoff: Enabling input asks the operating system for microphone access.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output
